summary: Duplicate function-call executions after SDK auto-reconnect when customer uses cookie-signed sessions and geo-routed webhooks
description: Issue summary: Customer reports repeated /duplicate/ function-tool invocations when their client loses connection and relies on the Python SDK auto-reconnect. The customer uses a cookie-signed session token pattern (session cookie contains a per-session nonce) and their callback webhook is geo-routed through an edge proxy that performs cookie rewriting. Impact: Duplicate side-effects (webhook created two DB rows, external payment webhook fired twice). Occurs intermittently during high client churn after a network blip and when requests are routed to a different region. Environment: Production (dedicated), us-east region; customer routes callbacks to a public webhook behind an edge CDN that rewrites cookies for regional affinity.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure the Python SDK to use auto-reconnect streaming with function-calling enabled and a server-side webhook that uses a signed session cookie for per-session nonce verification.
2) Set the edge proxy to perform cookie path/region rewrite (typical for geo-affinity).
3) Start a streaming session, trigger a function-call that causes an outbound webhook (e.g., create-payment intent).
4) Kill the client TCP connection (simulate flaky mobile), let the SDK auto-reconnect and replay inflight messages.
5) Observe webhook endpoint receives the callback twice and side-effects are created twice when the reconnect routes to a different edge node/region.
comments: 2026-03-10 15:10 - Support (Aisha Patel): Customer reports two identical payment intents created after mobile client reconnect. Provided request IDs and timestamps. Asked for SDK version and proxy topology.

2026-03-10 16:01 - Customer (Sarah Lim, FinWave): Using sdk-python v1.12.0, edge proxy is FastEdge CDN with region mapping. We see the webhook call twice only when client reconnects and the callback was routed to a different POP.

2026-03-10 16:40 - SRE (Ethan Morales): Reproduced in staging with synthetic traffic. Observed cookie rewrite changes session cookie value; server-side nonce validation accepts both because nonce persisted in session store, allowing duplicate acceptance on replayed callback.

2026-03-11 09:12 - SDK (Lin Guo): Noted that SDK currently replays in-flight function-call events after reconnect without attaching the original 'x-idempotency-key' header when resume crosses an edge boundary. Raising PR to preserve idempotency header on reconnect.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Support (Aisha Patel): Customer applied temporary workaround (see resolution). Monitoring for duplicates; no new duplicates in 24h.
investigation_notes: Edge proxy cookie rewrite can change session identifier suffix for geo affinity; this is expected behavior for their CDN.

Customer's webhook validates per-session nonce but does not enforce an idempotency-key header; therefore replays with same nonce are accepted as fresh if session id differs in cookie but nonce persisted server-side.
SDK auto-reconnect flow re-sends inflight events but in some cases (cross-region resume) does not reattach the original idempotency header that the platform normally provides for initial delivery.

We reproduced with sdk-python v1.12.0 and confirmed two independent factors: (a) header drop/preservation at reconnect, (b) webhook nonce acceptance logic that trusts persisted nonces across cookie variants.
Priority: high because customer observed financial side-effects (payment intents).
resolution: Workaround (applied 2026-03-11): Customer updated webhook to require strict idempotency-key header match in addition to session nonce; also disabled cookie rewrite rule for payment callbacks so POPs preserve original session cookie. Outcome: no duplicate webhooks observed in 24h. Engineering next steps: (1) SDK change to always preserve and re-send 'x-redwood-idempotency' header on reconnect/resume across regions (PR submitted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/398). (2) Runtime change to add a server-side guard that rejects duplicate function-call events without matching idempotency key (internal INT-981 opened). (3) Docs: add a new section explaining cookie-signed session pitfalls and recommended idempotency header enforcement for webhook handlers. ETA for SDK patch: 2026-03-18; ETA for runtime guard: 2026-03-25.
